questions.explanation: Raising the limits by 2.5x and 2x directly tackles the dwarfism syndrome: enterprises can now purchase sophisticated machinery and expand sales volumes without abruptly losing MSME credit guarantees, procurement quotas, and tax protections.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE):
1. It was jointly set up by the Ministry of MSME and the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).
2. It provides collateral-free credit guarantees to member lending institutions (MLIs).
3. Budget 2025-26 increases the maximum guarantee limit for MSEs to ₹10 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. CGTMSE was established by the Government of India and SIDBI. It provides credit guarantees so that commercial banks can disburse collateral-free loans to viable MSEs, with the cover ceiling now raised to ₹10 crore in Budget 2025-26.

questions.question: How much additional credit flow over a five-year horizon is projected to be stimulated by raising the MSE credit guarantee cover from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore in Budget 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The official PIB release states that expanding the credit guarantee cover to ₹10 crore will enable an additional credit flow of ₹1.5 lakh crore over five years for micro and small enterprises.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the concessional guarantee fee for startups in Budget 2025-26:
1. A reduced fee of 1% is applicable for startup loans in 27 priority sectors.
2. The guarantee cover for startups was expanded to a maximum of ₹20 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The budget package doubled the startup credit guarantee ceiling to ₹20 crore while lowering the guarantee fee to a concessional 1% across 27 designated priority sectors to lower the financial friction for innovative ventures.

questions.question: What is the term loan ceiling and eligibility duration under the Budget 2025-26 scheme for first-time women, SC, and ST entrepreneurs?
questions.explanation: The budget scheme provides term loans of up to ₹2 crore over a period of five years specifically targeted at 5 lakh first-time women, Scheduled Caste (SC), and Scheduled Tribe (ST) entrepreneurs.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the ₹5 lakh Customised Credit Card scheme for micro-enterprises:
1. It is exclusively available to micro-enterprises registered on the Udyam portal.
2. It provides short-term working capital liquidity to meet day-to-day business operating expenses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The customized credit card provides pre-approved, flexible short-term credit up to ₹5 lakh to micro-enterprises registered on Udyam, functioning as a rolling digital working capital line for inventory, raw materials, and utility payments.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund' operating under the Ministry of MSME?

options.A: A commercial real estate development trust
options.B: A fund-of-funds structure providing growth equity capital to viable, high-growth MSMEs to help them list on stock exchanges
options.C: A grant scheme paying monthly unemployment stipends
options.D: A foreign sovereign wealth fund investing in Indian sovereign debt

questions.explanation: The SRI Fund is an innovative Category-II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) Mother-Daughter fund structure. It injects patient growth equity into high-potential MSMEs to scale up into domestic and global champions and prepare them for listing on capital markets.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the performance of the Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund as cited in ForumIAS and Budget notes:
1. It has deployed over ₹15,442 crore across 682 high-growth enterprises.
2. Budget 2025-26 / FY27 policy frameworks propose an additional infusion of ₹2,000 crore into the SRI Fund alongside a ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct based on the ForumIAS text. The SRI Fund has successfully channeled ₹15,442 crore into 682 enterprises, and the latest budgetary approach infuses an additional ₹2,000 crore into SRI alongside the ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund.

questions.question: Why is the footwear and leather sector explicitly singled out for a 'Focus Product Scheme' in Budget 2025-26?

options.A: It has one of the highest employment generation ratios per crore of investment in the manufacturing sector
options.B: India imports 100% of all footwear components from North America
options.C: It is completely automated with zero requirement for human labor
options.D: Footwear production is legally restricted to CPSEs

questions.explanation: Footwear and leather manufacturing is an intensely labor-absorbing sector, employing a high percentage of women and disadvantaged artisans. The Focus Product Scheme aims to capitalize on this labor intensity, projecting 22 lakh new jobs and ₹4 lakh crore in turnover.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Toy Manufacturing Scheme announced in Budget 2025-26:
1. It emphasizes geographic cluster development and artisan skill-building.
2. It aims to position India as a competitive exporter in the global toy manufacturing supply chain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The scheme targets cluster-level testing facilities, electronic design capabilities, and quality standard compliance to help Indian toy clusters compete with East Asian exporters.

questions.question: Which agricultural region is specifically targeted for food processing capacity development through the establishment of NIFTEM in Bihar under Budget 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The PIB release explicitly notes that establishing NIFTEM in Bihar is aimed at boosting food processing industries and agro-entrepreneurship specifically in the Eastern region of India, enhancing post-harvest value addition and reducing farm wastage.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Manufacturing Mission highlighted in the MSME budget measures:
1. It provides policy support and strategic roadmaps for small, medium, and large industries under the Make in India initiative.
2. It places special emphasis on domestic clean technology manufacturing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The mission links small, medium, and large manufacturing players into an integrated ecosystem under Make in India, while driving targeted domestic manufacturing of clean technology components.

questions.question: In the budgetary outlay trends of the Ministry of MSME, how did the allocation change between 2019-20 (₹7,011.29 crore) and 2025-26 (₹23,168.15 crore)?

options.A: It decreased by 25% due to fiscal consolidation
options.B: It grew by more than 3.3 times (over 230% increase)
options.D: It grew by only 10% in nominal terms

questions.explanation: Comparing the official outlays in the PIB document: 2019-20 stood at ₹7,011.29 crore, while 2025-26 BE reached ₹23,168.15 crore—an increase of more than 3.3 times, reflecting the government's substantial budgetary commitment to MSME credit and infrastructure expansion.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: On which date was the 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme officially launched by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The PM Vishwakarma scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 and officially launched by the Prime Minister on September 17, 2023 (coinciding with Vishwakarma Jayanti) to support traditional artisans and craftspeople.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial architecture of the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by the Government of India.
2. It has an initial budgetary outlay of ₹13,000 crore for a period of five years (2023-24 to 2027-28).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct as specified in the PIB document: PM Vishwakarma is 100% funded by the Central Government as a Central Sector Scheme with an allocated outlay of ₹13,000 crore spanning 2023-24 to 2027-28.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: What is the primary target group of the PM Vishwakarma scheme?

options.A: Software engineers developing artificial intelligence applications
options.B: Traditional artisans and craftspeople who work with hands and tools across traditional trades
options.C: Commercial airline pilots and aeronautical mechanics

questions.explanation: The scheme specifically targets traditional artisans and craftspeople (Vishwakarmas) working with their hands and tools across 18 designated traditional family-based trades (such as carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, sculptors, cobblers, tailors, and masons).

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
According to the official PIB achievements data for PM Vishwakarma, consider the following statements:
1. Over 2.65 crore applications were submitted under the scheme.
2. Over 27.13 lakh applicants have been successfully registered.
3. Registered applicants undergo a 5-day 'Basic Training' program.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are exact milestones cited in the PIB document: over 2.65 crore applications received, 27.13 lakh successfully registered, with registered beneficiaries undergoing a mandatory 5-day (40 hours) basic skill training program.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: Under the PM Vishwakarma scheme, what daily training stipend is paid to registered artisans while attending the skill upgradation training?
questions.explanation: To compensate artisans for lost daily wage earnings while attending skill training, the scheme provides a daily stipend of ₹500 per day during the training period.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: What is the financial grant provided as a 'Toolkit Incentive' to beneficiaries under the PM Vishwakarma scheme upon completion of basic skill training?
questions.explanation: Beneficiaries who successfully complete the 5-day basic training receive a ₹15,000 toolkit incentive credited in the form of digital e-vouchers to enable them to purchase modern, high-precision tools and equipment.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the credit support provided under PM Vishwakarma:
1. Beneficiaries receive collateral-free enterprise development loans.
2. The credit is disbursed in two tranches: Tranche 1 up to ₹1,00,000 and Tranche 2 up to ₹2,00,000.
3. The loans are provided at a highly concessional interest rate of 5% to the beneficiary, with an 8% interest subvention paid by the Ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The scheme provides collateral-free enterprise credit: first tranche of ₹1 lakh (18 months repayment), followed by a second tranche of ₹2 lakh (30 months repayment) for standard accounts, at a fixed 5% interest rate charged to the artisan (with the Government absorbing up to 8% interest subvention).

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
With reference to the Udyam Registration Portal launched on July 1, 2020, consider the following statements:
1. It replaced the older systems of Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) and Entrepreneurs Memorandum-II (EM-II).
2. It operates on a paperless, self-declaration-based system with zero document upload requirements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The portal was launched on July 1, 2020, replacing UAM and EM-II. It enables seamless registration using PAN and Aadhaar without demanding physical documentation or registration fees.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: On which date was the 'Udyam Assist Platform' (UAP) officially introduced to bring informal micro-enterprises into the formal economic net?
questions.explanation: As recorded in the PIB document, the Government introduced the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) on November 11, 2023, specifically to bring Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) into the formal fold.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: What is the primary statutory benefit that Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) gain by registering on the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP)?

options.B: Access to commercial bank credit under Priority Sector Lending (PSL) norms
options.C: Free international travel for overseas trade fairs
options.D: Automatic listing on the National Stock Exchange

questions.explanation: The primary objective of UAP is to enable informal micro-enterprises that do not have GSTIN (being below the GST threshold) to obtain an Udyam Assist Certificate, making their borrowings from banks eligible for Priority Sector Lending (PSL) classification.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the integration of informal micro-enterprises via Udyam and Udyam Assist as cited in ForumIAS and PIB notes:
1. Udyam and Udyam Assist systematically shrink the informal shadow economy by creating verifiable enterprise identities.
2. As of February 4, 2025, over 5.93 crore registered MSMEs on Udyam employ over 25.18 crore people.
3. The vast majority of registered units on Udyam belong to the Medium enterprise category.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the official PIB document explicitly states that the vast majority of registered enterprises on the Udyam portal are classified as MICRO-enterprises, not Medium enterprises.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: Which identification document is mandatory for the authorized signatory/proprietor to initiate registration on the Udyam portal?
questions.explanation: Under the MSMED notification, an Aadhaar number is mandatory for registration on the Udyam portal: the Aadhaar of the proprietor for a proprietorship firm, of the managing partner for a partnership firm, and of a karta in the case of a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF).

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the dynamic updating of MSME classification on the Udyam portal:
1. The portal automatically updates an enterprise's investment and turnover data based on its filed Income Tax Returns and GST returns.
2. An enterprise does not need to submit fresh manual declarations every year to maintain its registration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Udyam's digital backend pulls audited WDV investment figures from CBDT database and turnover from GSTN, dynamically updating the enterprise's status without manual bureaucratic interventions.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: How many traditional trades are covered under the scope of the PM Vishwakarma scheme?
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma provides comprehensive support to artisans and craftspeople engaged across 18 traditional trades, including carpentry, boat making, armoury, blacksmithing, hammer and toolkit making, lock-smithing, sculpting/stone-carving, goldsmithing, pottery, cobbling/footwear making, masonry, basket/mat/broom weaving, doll and toy making, barbering, garland making, washerman trade, tailoring, and fishing net making.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the digital transaction incentive under the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. Beneficiaries receive a cash incentive of ₹1 per digital transaction for up to 100 eligible digital transactions per month.
2. This incentive aims to promote digital financial literacy and adoption of digital payments among grassroots artisans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The scheme provides ₹1 per digital transaction (up to 100 transactions per month, i.e., ₹100/month credited directly into the artisan's bank account) to incentivize digital payment acceptance among traditional craftspeople.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: What is the fee charged by the Government of India for registering an enterprise on the official Udyam portal?

options.B: ₹500 for micro and ₹2,500 for medium enterprises

questions.explanation: Udyam registration is 100% free of cost. The Ministry of MSME has repeatedly warned against fraudulent private commercial websites charging fees for Udyam registration.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the verification and approval process under the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. Enrolment is conducted through Common Services Centres (CSCs).
2. Applications undergo a three-stage verification process: Gram Panchayat / Urban Local Body level, District Implementation Committee level, and Screening Committee level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Artisans apply through biometric authentication at Common Services Centres (CSCs). Verification involves a rigorous three-tier vetting process starting at the local Gram Panchayat/ULB level, passing through the District Committee, and finalized by the State Screening Committee.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an eligible trade under the PM Vishwakarma scheme?
questions.explanation: Software Quality Assurance Analyst is a modern white-collar IT profession, whereas PM Vishwakarma is strictly designed for 18 traditional hands-and-tools artisan trades.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding marketing support provided under the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. Artisans are provided onboarding support onto the Government e-Marketplace (GeM).
2. The scheme supports quality certification, branding, and linkage to e-commerce platforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. In addition to skilling and credit, PM Vishwakarma actively links artisans with national and global markets through GeM onboarding, quality certification, packaging support, and participation in trade exhibitions.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: What document is provided to an artisan upon registration under PM Vishwakarma that certifies their traditional craft identity?

options.A: PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card

questions.explanation: Registered beneficiaries receive a formal PM Vishwakarma Certificate and a digitally verified PM Vishwakarma ID Card acknowledging them as recognized artisans.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) ecosystem:
1. Designated Agencies (such as Banks, NBFCs, and Microfinance Institutions) act as assisting agencies to onboard informal micro-enterprises onto UAP.
2. The initiative addresses the structural barrier wherein lack of GST registration previously excluded micro-borrowers from formal priority credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Financial intermediaries (banks, MFIs) act as Designated Agencies to gather basic details from their micro-borrowers and upload them to UAP, allowing entities exempted from mandatory GST to obtain formal recognition for Priority Sector Lending (PSL).

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: In the Mindmap notes, what total registration figure on Udyam is cited for August 2026?

options.C: 9.16 crore MSMEs employing over 20 crore people

questions.explanation: The Mindmap notes under Data explicitly state: 'Aug 2026 -> 9.16 cr MSMEs regd on udyam portal employing >20 cr people', representing the projected formalization footprint of the portal.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the repayment tenure for enterprise development loans under PM Vishwakarma:
1. The First Tranche of up to ₹1 lakh has a repayment period of 18 months.
2. The Second Tranche of up to ₹2 lakh has a repayment period of 30 months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The loan architecture is tiered: Tranche 1 provides working capital up to ₹1 lakh for 18 months; upon maintaining a standard repayment track record, the artisan is eligible for Tranche 2 up to ₹2 lakh with a 30-month repayment horizon.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question: Under PM Vishwakarma, what is the prerequisite for an artisan to become eligible for the second credit tranche of ₹2 lakh?

options.A: The artisan must incorporate a public limited company
options.B: The artisan must have maintained a standard loan account under the first tranche and adopted digital transactions or completed advanced training
options.C: The artisan must pledge immovable property as mortgage
options.D: The artisan must export 50% of their output to European markets

questions.explanation: To qualify for the Second Tranche (up to ₹2 lakh), the beneficiary must maintain a standard repayment record for the first tranche loan for at least 6 months, demonstrate adoption of digital transactions, or undergo the optional advanced training.

questions.module: PM Vishwakarma, Udyam & Udyam Assist Platform
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the age and family eligibility criteria under the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. The minimum age of the beneficiary must be 18 years on the date of registration.
2. The benefits under the scheme are restricted to one member of a family (defined as husband, wife, and unmarried children).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Eligibility guidelines stipulate a minimum age of 18 years, active engagement in one of the 18 traditional trades, and a strict rule limiting scheme benefits to only one member per family to ensure broad equitable coverage across artisan households.

questions.question: What is the maximum admissible project cost for setting up a new enterprise in the manufacturing sector under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
questions.explanation: Under PMEGP, the maximum project cost admissible for establishing a new unit in the manufacturing sector is ₹50 lakh (raised from the earlier ₹25 lakh ceiling), while for the service sector it is ₹20 lakh.

questions.question: What is the maximum admissible project cost for setting up a new enterprise in the service sector under PMEGP?
questions.explanation: Under PMEGP guidelines, the maximum admissible project cost for setting up a new business in the service or business sector is ₹20 lakh.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the margin money subsidy rates under PMEGP for General Category applicants:
1. 15% of the project cost in urban areas.
2. 25% of the project cost in rural areas.
3. The beneficiary's own contribution is 10% of the project cost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. For General Category applicants under PMEGP, the beneficiary contributes 10% of the project cost as equity, while the Government provides a margin money subsidy of 15% in urban areas and 25% in rural areas.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the subsidy structure under PMEGP for Special Category beneficiaries (SC, ST, OBC, Women, Transgenders, etc.):
1. The margin money subsidy is 25% in urban areas.
2. The margin money subsidy is 35% in rural areas.
3. The beneficiary's own contribution is restricted to only 5% of the project cost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. For Special Categories, the required beneficiary contribution is reduced to just 5%, while the Government provides an enhanced margin money subsidy of 25% in urban areas and 35% in rural areas.

questions.question:
Which of the following groups/regions were specifically included in the 'Special Category' under PMEGP in recent developments as noted by PIB?
1. Units in Aspirational Districts
2. Transgenders
3. High-Net-Worth Individuals
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The official PIB document highlights that in a notable recent development, units located in Aspirational Districts and Transgender entrepreneurs have been explicitly incorporated into the Special Category to access enhanced 25%/35% subsidies.

questions.question: What technological innovation has been initiated for PMEGP units to capture product details and create direct market linkages as per official notes?

options.A: Mandatory installation of facial recognition CCTV cameras
options.B: Geo-tagging of all funded PMEGP units
options.D: Satellite tracking of daily worker attendance

questions.explanation: As cited in the PIB document, geo-tagging of PMEGP units has been initiated to capture the exact physical location, product details, and production capacities of units, facilitating traceability, quality monitoring, and market linkages.

questions.question: What training is provided free of cost to prospective entrepreneurs under PMEGP before or after project sanction?
questions.explanation: Prospective entrepreneurs under PMEGP receive a free 2-day Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training to equip them with foundational business planning, accounting, and compliance knowledge.

questions.question:
According to the official PIB achievements for PMEGP in 2023-24, consider the following statements:
1. PMEGP supported 89,118 micro-enterprises across various sectors.
2. The scheme disbursed ₹3,093.87 crore as margin money subsidy.
3. It generated an estimated 7,12,944 employment opportunities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are exact achievements recorded in the PIB document for FY 2023-24: 89,118 enterprises supported, ₹3,093.87 crore margin money subsidy disbursed, generating 7,12,944 jobs.

questions.question: Which statutory organization serves as the single National Nodal Agency for implementing PMEGP at the national level?

options.C: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
options.D: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

questions.explanation: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), a statutory body under the Ministry of MSME, is the national nodal agency implementing PMEGP across the country.

questions.question:
With reference to the Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI), consider the following statements:
1. It was originally launched in 2005-06 and comprehensively revamped in 2014-15.
2. Its primary objective is to organize traditional artisans and industries into clusters to improve competitiveness and product marketability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. SFURTI was launched in 2005-06 and revamped in 2014-15. It organizes traditional artisans into sustainable geographic collectives and clusters to upgrade their technology, establish Common Facility Centres (CFCs), and increase earnings.

questions.question:
Regarding the official milestones of SFURTI as of December 12, 2024 (cited in the PIB release), consider the following statements:
1. Since 2014-15, SFURTI has approved the formation of 513 clusters.
2. Exactly 376 clusters have successfully become functional.
3. A total grant of ₹1,336 crore has been extended, generating sustainable employment for around 2,20,800 artisans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are exact milestones documented in the PIB release: 513 clusters approved, 376 functional, ₹1,336 crore grants disbursed, supporting 2,20,800 artisans.

questions.question: What is the mandatory minimum percentage of annual procurement that Central Ministries, Departments, and CPSEs must source from Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) under the Public Procurement Policy?
questions.explanation: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) notified in 2012 (and revised in 2018), Central Ministries, Government Departments, and Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) must mandatorily procure at least 25% of their total annual purchases of goods and services from MSEs.

questions.question:
Within the overall 25% mandatory annual public procurement target from MSEs, what specific sub-targets are earmarked for disadvantaged entrepreneur groups?
1. 4 per cent is earmarked for MSEs owned by Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST).
2. 3 per cent is earmarked for MSEs owned by Women entrepreneurs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Within the overarching 25% quota, the policy establishes targeted sub-allocations: 4% reserved for SC/ST-owned MSEs and 3% reserved exclusively for Women-owned MSEs.

questions.question: How many items are exclusively reserved for procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises under the Public Procurement Policy?
questions.explanation: As explicitly specified in the official PIB document, exactly 358 items are exclusively reserved for procurement from MSEs by all central government buyers, ensuring protected domestic demand for traditional small-scale manufacturing products.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the performance of the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs in the fiscal year 2023-24:
1. Total procurement by Central Ministries, Departments, and CPSEs from MSEs was ₹74,717 crore.
2. This procurement constituted 43.71% of their total annual procurement, substantially exceeding the 25% mandate.
3. The procurement directly benefited 2,58,413 MSEs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are exact achievements recorded in the PIB document: ₹74,717 crore procured from MSEs in 2023-24, achieving an impressive 43.71% share (well above the 25% statutory target) and benefiting 2,58,413 MSE enterprises.

questions.question: Which portal was launched by the Ministry of MSME to monitor the public procurement of goods and services from MSEs by CPSEs?
questions.explanation: The MSME Sambandh Portal is the designated public procurement monitoring portal where CPSEs report their monthly and annual procurement progress from MSEs, tracking adherence to the 25%, 4% (SC/ST), and 3% (Women) quotas.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding tender benefits provided to MSEs under the Public Procurement Policy:
1. MSEs are provided tender sets free of cost.
2. MSEs are exempt from the payment of Earnest Money Deposit (EMD).
3. In tenders where an MSE quotes within a price band of L1 + 15%, the MSE is allowed to supply a portion of the requirement by matching the L1 price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. The policy grants MSEs free tender documents, EMD waivers, and a price-matching preference (within the L1 + 15% band, MSEs can supply up to 25% of the tender order by matching the lowest L1 quote from a non-MSE).

questions.question: Under SFURTI, what is the core infrastructure established within an artisan cluster to provide access to shared high-value machinery?
questions.explanation: The core infrastructure funded under SFURTI is the Common Facility Centre (CFC), which houses expensive specialized processing machinery, design software, and quality testing labs that individual artisans could never afford independently.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the implementation architecture of PMEGP at the state and district levels:
1. State KVIC Directorates implement PMEGP in rural areas.
2. District Industries Centres (DICs) implement PMEGP in both rural and urban areas.
3. State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs) participate in implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. While KVIC is the single national agency, state-level implementation is decentralized across State KVIC Directorates, State KVIBs, and District Industries Centres (DICs), with financing channeled through commercial and regional rural banks.

questions.question: What is the minimum educational qualification required for a beneficiary applying for a PMEGP project costing above ₹10 lakh in manufacturing or above ₹5 lakh in services?
questions.explanation: Under PMEGP guidelines, for projects costing above ₹10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and above ₹5 lakh in the business/service sector, the beneficiary must possess a minimum educational qualification of at least having passed 8th standard.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Second Loan for Upgradation' under PMEGP for well-performing existing units:
1. Existing PMEGP units that have repaid their initial bank loans successfully can apply for a second loan for technological upgradation.
2. The maximum project cost for upgradation is up to ₹1 crore for manufacturing and up to ₹25 lakh for services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. To address the problem of dwarfism, PMEGP introduced a Second Loan component for existing high-performing units to expand: up to ₹1 crore for manufacturing units and up to ₹25 lakh for service units, with a 15% subsidy (20% for NER/Hills).

questions.question: Under the Public Procurement Policy, what qualifies an enterprise as 'owned by SC/ST' or 'owned by Women'?

options.A: At least 10% of employees must belong to SC/ST or Women
options.B: In case of proprietary MSE, the proprietor must be SC/ST or Woman; in partnership, at least 51% share must be held by SC/ST or Women partners
options.C: The enterprise must have its registered factory in a tribal area
options.D: The board of directors must include a government civil servant

questions.explanation: Under the policy definitions, an MSE is considered owned by SC/ST or Women if: (a) for proprietary concerns, the sole proprietor is SC/ST or Woman; (b) for partnership enterprises, at least 51% shareholding is held by SC/ST or Women; (c) for private limited companies, at least 51% of equity shares are held by SC/ST or Women.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional objectives of the RAMP scheme:
1. It facilitates capacity building of State MSME departments to develop State Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs).
2. It supports MSMEs in achieving Green/ZED (Zero Defect Zero Effect) certification.
3. It is funded partially via a loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because RAMP is funded by the World Bank (IBRD), not the International Monetary Fund (IMF). It aims to improve Centre-State coordination through Strategic Investment Plans and promotes ZED environmental certification.

questions.question: What happens if a CPSE fails to meet the 4% procurement target from SC/ST-owned MSEs or 3% from Women-owned MSEs in a given financial year?

options.A: The CPSE's operating license is automatically suspended
options.B: The shortfall must be reported on the MSME Sambandh portal, and the CPSE must provide detailed justifications in its annual report
options.C: The CPSE directors are subjected to mandatory criminal prosecution
options.D: The CPSE must transfer 50% of its profits to private micro-enterprises

questions.explanation: Procurement performance is monitored transparently on the MSME Sambandh portal and reviewed at the Cabinet Secretariat and Parliamentary Committee level. Any shortfall must be officially reported, justified, and accounted for in the annual performance evaluation (MoU ratings) of CPSEs.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements comparing SFURTI and PMEGP:
1. PMEGP focuses primarily on individual enterprise creation in the non-farm sector.
2. SFURTI focuses on collective cluster-based regeneration of traditional village industries and artisan guilds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. PMEGP is primarily an individual beneficiary-oriented scheme supporting micro-enterprise creation via bank credit and margin money subsidies. SFURTI, by contrast, is a cluster-level collective development intervention focused on traditional crafts, common facility centers, and artisan clusters.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: Which Union Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is cited in the Mindmap notes regarding the focus on grassroots rural industrialization and marginalized community empowerment?
questions.explanation: Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi is specifically referenced in the Mindmap notes under 'VIEWS', advocating for targeted rural enterprise creation, upliftment of marginalized artisans (SC/ST/women), and scaling up micro-units into sustainable ventures.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the critique of Indian industrial policy articulated by renowned management thinker and former Planning Commission member Arun Maira:
1. He emphasizes the need to avoid the trap of 'more factories, but not more jobs for people'.
2. He argues that subsidizing capital over labor leads enterprises to substitute workers with automation even in a labor-surplus economy.
3. He advocates for institutional redesign that promotes worker voice, collective enterprise, and labor-absorbing manufacturing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements accurately summarize Arun Maira's core economic philosophy as cited in the notes: capital subsidies incentivize firms to adopt automated machinery instead of hiring workers, resulting in jobless growth. He urges policy to prioritize labor absorption and human dignity.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: Which senior administrative official is cited in the Mindmap notes as driving digital integration, paperless Udyam expansion, and cash-flow credit reforms in the Ministry of MSME?
questions.explanation: Bharat Khera, Secretary in the Ministry of MSME, is referenced in the Mindmap notes under administrative views, emphasizing digital formalization, easing the compliance burden, and transitioning from collateral-based lending to cash-flow credit assessment.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
With reference to the seminal economic study by Chang-Tai Hsieh and Peter J. Klenow ('Misallocation and Manufacturing TFP in China and India') cited in the notes, consider the following statements:
1. Resource misallocation of capital and labor across manufacturing plants in India lowers aggregate manufacturing Total Factor Productivity (TFP) by 40 to 60 per cent compared to the United States.
2. In India, a 40-year-old manufacturing plant is barely larger in employment and output than an infant plant, due to distortionary size-dependent policies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Hsieh & Klenow's landmark study demonstrated that policy distortions and credit market frictions in India misallocate resources to unproductive units, reducing national TFP by 40-60%. Furthermore, while a typical US plant grows eight-fold over 40 years, an Indian plant barely doubles in size, illustrating institutionalized dwarfism.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What is the primary finding of the academic research by Santana & Joseph referenced in the Mindmap notes on small enterprise competitiveness?

options.A: MSMEs should completely stop adopting digital technologies
options.B: Indian small enterprises suffer from systemic technological capability deficits, low R&D investment, and weak inter-firm knowledge spillovers within clusters
options.C: Indian small enterprises have higher patent output than Silicon Valley startups
options.D: All small manufacturing should be relocated to coastal islands

questions.explanation: Studies by Santana & Joseph analyze the innovation systems and technological backwardness of Indian small enterprises, highlighting that low internal R&D expenditure and weak cluster linkages prevent them from transitioning from low-value imitation to frontier technology.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
With reference to the research by agricultural economists Ashok Gulati & S. Rao cited in the notes, consider the following statements:
1. They emphasize the vital role of Agro-MSMEs in connecting rural farm producers with high-value urban food processing markets.
2. They advocate for investments in post-harvest cold chain logistics, food testing labs, and rural agro-processing clusters to reduce farm wastage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Gulati & Rao's work emphasizes that rural agro-processing MSMEs are the key bridge for doubling farmer incomes: by building modern cold chains and agro-clusters, they convert perishable farm produce into shelf-stable, high-value consumer goods.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: Which domestic manufacturing cluster is featured in the Mindmap case studies as a prime example of successful geographic concentration and specialized artisan labor?

options.A: The Jalandhar - Meerut sports goods cluster
options.C: The Pune - Chakan automobile assembly line
options.D: The Bokaro - Rourkela blast furnace belt

questions.explanation: The Jalandhar-Meerut sports cluster is the specific case study in the notes, highlighting how artisan tradition, localized subcontracting, and shared tooling allow small firms to capture substantial global export market share in cricket bats, balls, and athletic equipment.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the German 'Mittelstand' model cited in the case studies:
1. Mittelstand firms are typically mid-sized, privately owned, and pursue long-term generational growth rather than quarterly stock market profits.
2. They focus on narrow, specialized B2B niches where they become indispensable global market leaders ('Hidden Champions').
3. They invest heavily in employee apprenticeships and continuous incremental product refinement (Kaizen).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements accurately capture the Mittelstand blueprint. These firms avoid diversification, focusing instead on being the world's best in a hyper-specialized component (valves, lasers, printing presses), sustained by dual vocational schooling and patient family capital.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What is the primary policy lesson that Indian policymakers draw from the German Mittelstand model?

options.A: India should ban all large multi-national corporations
options.B: India needs to cultivate mid-sized manufacturing champions that specialize in niche engineering, rather than remaining trapped in micro-survivalism
options.C: India should eliminate all technical vocational schooling
options.D: India should nationalize all small engineering workshops

questions.explanation: The core policy lesson from the Mittelstand is that an industrial nation cannot rely solely on a few giant conglomerates or millions of tiny informal shops: it needs a strong middle tier of 100-500 employee engineering champions producing high-precision, export-grade components.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
According to the Mindmap notes, what are the four key policy suggestions to unleash the MSME sector?
1. Bridge the credit gap
2. Eradicate regulatory penalty
3. Comprehensive policy reforms (such as correcting Inverted Duty Structure)
4. Create 'more factories, not people' by eliminating compliance cliffs
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The Mindmap notes under 'SUGGESTIONS' explicitly list: (1) bridge the credit gap, (2) eradicate regulatory penalty, (3) policy reforms, and (4) more factories not people (solving the employment paradox by making it painless for factories to add formal workers).

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: How does the 'Becker's Deterrence' economic framework apply to resolving delayed payments and regulatory enforcement in the MSME sector?

options.A: Harsh penal laws (such as compound interest) fail to deter large buyers if the probability of detection and speed of adjudication remain near-zero
options.B: All corporate buyers must be sentenced to mandatory prison terms upon any default
options.C: Interest rates should be reduced to zero to eliminate buyer resistance
options.D: Courts should refuse to hear any commercial payment disputes

questions.explanation: Gary Becker's economic model of deterrence posits that Expected Penalty = Severity × Probability of Detection × Speed. Even though Section 16 mandates severe compound interest at 3x Bank Rate, if the probability of an MSE filing a case is low (due to fear of business loss) and adjudication takes years, buyers continue delaying payments with impunity.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Missing Middle' and firm productivity:
1. Mid-sized enterprises are typically more productive and pay higher wages than micro-enterprises.
2. Mid-sized enterprises have greater capacity to absorb technological innovations and comply with global ESG and quality standards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Empirical evidence shows that scaling from micro to medium size unlocks economies of scale, allows hiring of professional management, enables investment in worker safety, and facilitates compliance with stringent global supply chain standards.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: In the analysis by Ashok Chandra in ForumIAS, what is described as the 'defining challenge for India's banking sector in the Viksit Bharat decade'?

options.B: Narrowing the persistent MSME financing gap through cash-flow-based lending and digital infrastructure
options.C: Replacing all commercial bank branches with post office savings counters

questions.explanation: The ForumIAS text explicitly states: 'Yet the financing gap persists and narrowing it is the defining challenge for India's banking sector in the Viksit Bharat decade.' This requires moving from physical collateral to cash-flow lending using GST data and Account Aggregators.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of Account Aggregators (AAs) in expanding MSME credit access:
1. Account Aggregators allow MSME borrowers to digitally and securely share verifiable bank statements and financial data with prospective lenders.
2. Lenders can evaluate cash-flow health in real time without demanding notarized paper balance sheets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The RBI-regulated Account Aggregator (AA) framework enables consent-based, encrypted sharing of financial information, allowing banks to assess working capital health instantly and approve cash-flow loans in minutes.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: Why is the cluster approach (like SFURTI and Toy Clusters) considered superior to supporting isolated, scattered micro-enterprises?

options.A: Clusters make it illegal for enterprises to compete against each other
options.B: Clusters enable shared infrastructure (Common Facility Centers), bulk raw material procurement discounts, and collective brand visibility
options.C: Clusters eliminate all electricity and transportation costs
options.D: Clusters mandate that all profits are pooled into the state treasury

questions.explanation: Isolated micro-units lack capital for specialized testing labs, design studios, or bulk procurement. Cluster agglomeration enables shared Common Facility Centers (CFCs), bulk raw material purchasing, collective branding, and specialized supplier networks, reducing overhead costs.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the external sector headwinds identified in the Mindmap notes:
1. Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) like strict sanitary, phytosanitary, and carbon border regulations disproportionately hurt MSMEs due to high compliance testing costs.
2. Global macroeconomic shocks and freight rate spikes squeeze thin profit margins in small exporting firms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Small exporters operate on razor-thin operating margins. Complex foreign regulatory standards (e.g. EU CBAM, technical packaging norms) and sudden freight rate volatility hit MSMEs far harder than large conglomerates that have specialized trade compliance legal departments.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What is the primary barrier that prevents small enterprises from investing in workforce skill development, leading to the 'Skill Challenge' noted in the Mindmap?

options.A: Employees are legally forbidden from learning new skills
options.B: Firms fear that after spending resources training a worker, the worker will be poached by larger competitors (the free-rider problem)
options.C: Vocational training is banned by state industrial departments

questions.explanation: In small enterprise economics, the poaching/free-rider problem is a well-known market failure: small employers hesitate to invest in formal employee skilling because trained workers frequently leave for marginally higher wages at competing firms, leaving the small firm with unrecoverable training costs.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jan Samarth Portal:
1. It serves as a unified digital platform connecting beneficiaries directly to lenders across multiple credit-linked government schemes.
2. It facilitates end-to-end digital processing and in-principle loan approvals for MSME borrowers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The Jan Samarth portal is a common electronic platform linking 13+ credit-linked government subsidies and schemes across agriculture, livelihood, education, and business, enabling seamless digital loan applications and instant in-principle sanctions.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What strategic role do MSMEs play in domestic supply chain resilience and national defense manufacturing?

options.A: They act as tier-2 and tier-3 component suppliers and specialized machining contractors for defense public sector undertakings
options.C: They are restricted to manufacturing office stationery only
options.D: They replace the armed forces in border security

questions.explanation: In strategic industries, large prime contractors and Defense PSUs (like HAL, BEL) depend on thousands of precision MSMEs for specialized tooling, precision sub-assemblies, electronic harnesses, and specialized alloys, making MSME capability critical for strategic sovereignty.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Social Inclusion' dimension of the MSME sector in India:
1. Over 60 per cent of MSMEs in India are owned by individuals belonging to SC, ST, and Other Backward Classes (OBC).
2. Targeted schemes like PM Vishwakarma and PMEGP Special Category quotas directly direct financial capital to traditionally marginalized artisanal communities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. MSMEs are the primary vehicle of grassroots affirmative economic empowerment: national surveys establish that the vast majority of micro-enterprises are run by OBC, SC, ST, and women entrepreneurs who lack access to corporate boardrooms.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What is the core distinction between 'Survivalist Micro-Enterprises' and 'Transformational Small Enterprises'?

options.A: Survivalist units seek daily subsistence income with little innovation; transformational enterprises reinvest profits, adopt technology, and scale employment
options.B: Survivalist enterprises have foreign venture capital funding
options.C: Transformational enterprises are legally required to operate at a financial loss
options.D: Survivalist enterprises employ thousands of workers

questions.explanation: Economic literature distinguishes 'own-account survivalists' (who start a tiny shop because no formal jobs exist, generating subsistence income without scaling) from 'transformational entrepreneurs' (who innovate, hire non-family workers, reinvest surpluses, and build scalable manufacturing enterprises).

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of MSMEs in regional industrial decentralization:
1. Large-scale capital-intensive heavy industries tend to cluster around metropolitan ports and mineral belts.
2. MSMEs have low threshold capital requirements, allowing non-metro Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns to develop diverse manufacturing bases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Heavy industries are constrained by massive capital, mineral logistics, and power grids, leading to regional geographic concentration. MSMEs, by contrast, can be seeded across semi-urban and rural districts, creating local jobs and countering regional disparities.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: According to the ForumIAS conclusion, what kind of ecosystem is imperative for building a developed and inclusive India?

options.B: A vibrant, digitally enabled, financially empowered and globally connected MSME ecosystem
options.C: An economy completely devoid of small private businesses
options.D: An economy that relies solely on service sector exports

questions.explanation: The conclusion of the ForumIAS text emphasizes: 'A vibrant, digitally enabled, financially empowered and globally connected MSME ecosystem will be imperative for building a developed and inclusive India.'

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the transition of Indian MSMEs into global supply chains:
1. The share of MSME-related products in India's total exports has consistently exceeded 45 per cent in recent years.
2. Achieving Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED) quality certification is critical for Indian MSMEs to meet European and American environmental supply chain mandates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. MSMEs generate nearly 46-48% of total exports. With major importers implementing strict quality and environmental standards (ZED / CBAM), achieving high quality with zero environmental impact is essential for sustaining export competitiveness.

questions.module: Expert Views, Academic Studies & Case Studies
questions.question: What is the overarching vision of India's MSME policy reforms as encapsulated in the provided notes?

options.A: To force all small enterprises to permanently shut down operations
options.B: To transition from informal to formal, from small-scale production to value-added manufacturing, from local markets to global value chains, and from survival-led to technology-led competitiveness
options.C: To replace all manufacturing with foreign imported products
options.D: To mandate that all enterprises must be owned by municipal corporations

questions.explanation: The ultimate strategic vision articulated across the ForumIAS, Mindmap, and PIB documents is the multi-dimensional transition of India's MSME sector: from informal to formal, from small-scale production to value-added manufacturing, from local markets to global value chains, and from survival-led enterprise to technology-led competitiveness.
